title: How we built saga rollbacks for Cloudflare Workflows
partialText: Cloudflare Workflows, our durable execution engine for multi-step applications, now supports saga-style rollbacks, allowing developers to specify a compensating action for each step.do().

title: Unlocking the Cloudflare app ecosystem with OAuth for all
partialText: Self-Managed OAuth is now available to all developers on Cloudflare. Here's how we executed a zero-downtime migration of our core OAuth engine to make it happen.

title: The post-quantum EO is an important milestone. Now it’s time to get to work
partialText: The new post-quantum executive order sets a 2030 migration deadline and establishes a powerful foundation for post-quantum resilience. We look at what it gets right, where it can go further, and our migration playbook for government and industry.

title: How we found a bug in the hyper HTTP library
partialText: By rearchitecting the Images binding, we accidentally uncovered a bug that existed in the open-source hyper library across multiple major versions.

title: Temporary Cloudflare Accounts for AI agents
partialText: The moment an agent needs to deploy something, it slams face-first into a wall built for humans. Today we're rolling out Temporary Accounts on Cloudflare Workers. Any agent can now run wrangler deploy — temporary and get a live Worker in seconds.

title: Build your own vulnerability harness
partialText: We break down the technical architecture behind our multi-stage vulnerability discovery harness and automated triage loop. Learn how we manage state controls, squash false positives through adversarial review, and route around LLM context limits.

title: Celebrating 12 years of Project Galileo
partialText: To mark the 12th anniversary of Project Galileo, Cloudflare has released its first comprehensive report analyzing cyberattacks against civil society.

title: Bringing more agent harnesses and frameworks to Cloudflare, starting with Flue
partialText: The Agents SDK is now a runtime any agent framework can build on. Today we're opening up the Agents SDK primitives, with Flue as a first framework targeting Agents SDK, and rolling out agents in the dashboard.

title: Introducing the Cloudflare One stack: agent-powered deployment
partialText: The Cloudflare One stack is a library of agent skills that gives any AI agent the knowledge it needs to plan, deploy, and manage a Zero Trust environment — no migration calls required.

title: Cloudflare DMARC Management is now generally available
partialText: Get unified visibility into your email authentication posture and reach full DMARC enforcement with deeper reporting, record analysis, and SPF audits free for every Cloudflare customer.

title: Growing the Cloudflare AI team with talent from Ensemble AI
partialText: Cloudflare is deepening our investment in AI with the addition of team members from Ensemble AI, focusing on machine learning infrastructure and efficiency.

title: Scaling Security Insights: how we achieved a 10x increase in global scanning capacity
partialText: Cloudflare Security Insights system now processes over 120 scans per second, providing frequent insights for all customers. By optimizing Kafka consumers, Postgres queries, and our API, we scaled our throughput 10x without adding hardware.

title: Route public traffic to private applications with Cloudflare
partialText: Application Services for Private Origins is available now in closed beta. Route public hostnames to private IP origins over your existing IPsec, GRE, CNI, or Cloudflare Mesh paths. No public IPs or extra connector software required.

title: Defend against frontier cyber models: Cloudflare's architecture as customer zero
partialText: In our post about Project Glasswing, we made the argument that the architecture around a vulnerability matters more than the speed of the patch. Here we walk through what that architecture looks like, the threats it defends against, and how we run it ourselves as Cloudflare's customer zero.

title: Turning Cloudflare’s threat indicators into real-time WAF rules
partialText: Cloudflare customers can now use Cloudforce One threat intelligence directly within the WAF to block high-risk traffic. By using new cf.intel fields, security teams can automate protection against specific threat actors and targeted industries in real time.

title: Your AI bill is out of control. Cloudflare can fix it now.
partialText: AI Gateway now features real-time spend limits to prevent runaway token bills across multiple AI providers. By integrating with Cloudflare Access, companies can use identity-driven budgets and policies.

title: VoidZero is joining Cloudflare
partialText: VoidZero, the team behind Vite, Vitest, Rolldown, Oxc, and Vite+, is joining Cloudflare. Vite stays open source, vendor-agnostic, and built for everyone.

title: Enforcing the First AS in BGP AS_PATHs
partialText: BGP is vulnerable to routing hijacks and path leaks that negatively impact traffic on the Internet. RPKI helps solve some of these problems, but for some forged paths, we need to rely on a simpler mechanism: First AS enforcement in BGP.

title: How we reduced core unit boot time from hours to minutes
partialText: We investigated why firmware updates were causing our core servers to take four hours to reboot. By diving into UEFI data structures and iPXE automation, we eliminated unnecessary timeouts and cut boot times back down to minutes.

title: How we built Cloudflare's data platform and an AI agent on top of it
partialText: Here’s how we built Town Lake, Cloudflare's unified analytics platform, alongside Skipper, an internal AI agent running on top of it.
